summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of ileocolonic Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis, was admitted for recurrent right lower quadrant abdominal pain and non-bloody diarrhea, consistent with a previous steroid-responsive flare. He had 30 small-volume bowel movements over two days. Labs showed normal white count, CRP, and ESR, with mildly low bicarbonate. IV methylprednisolone and fluids were initiated. The patient expressed concern about steroid type, preferring hydrocortisone, but was informed that methylprednisolone was equivalent and standard. He became frustrated with care, insisted on leaving, and discharged against medical advice. He refused a prescription for prednisone 50mg daily and follow-up instructions. A concurrent left great toe fracture was noted, with ortho recommending continued conservative management in a walking shoe.
